name: checkcite
description: Verify the citations in a scientific paper. Given a paper (PDF, LaTeX, BibTeX, or plain text), returns one verdict per reference along two independent dimensions: a metadata-driven top-level verdict (VALID / FABRICATED / UNVERIFIABLE) and a claim-support dimension (SUPPORTED / CONTRADICTS / NEUTRAL / UNVERIFIABLE) telling whether the cited paper actually supports the citing sentence. Each verdict travels with the evidence trail that produced it — databases checked, metadata comparison, retrieved passages from the cited paper, and the verifier's reasoning.

operations.summary: Verify all citations in a scientific paper (synchronous).
operations.description: Runs the full three-layer CheckCite pipeline synchronously and returns the full report. Best for small papers (<30 references) and demos. For long papers, clients that cannot hold the HTTP connection open, or anything that must survive a refresh, prefer the async flow (submit_job / get_job).

mode.description: 'quick' runs only the deterministic existence + metadata layers (free). 'agentic' additionally runs the LLM-based semantic verification layer.

retry_failed.description: Clear NOT_FOUND cache and retry references that previously failed existence lookup.

returns.description: List of per-reference verdicts with evidence trails; see the OpenAPI spec at `/api/v1/openapi.json` for the full schema.

operations.summary: Submit a paper for asynchronous verification.
operations.description: Queues the verification pipeline as a background job and returns a `job_id` immediately (HTTP 202). The response also carries a `status_url` the client can poll. Jobs persist to disk, so they survive browser refreshes, client disconnects, and brief server restarts.

operations.summary: Fetch the status and (if ready) result of an async job.
operations.description: Safe to call repeatedly. Poll every 1-3 seconds until `status` is `done` or `failed`. When `done`, the full PaperReport is available under `result`.

returns.description: `{job_id, status: queued|running|done|failed, stage, progress, input_info, result?, error?}`.

operations.summary: Delete a completed or failed job record.

returns.description: Self-describing metadata so an agent framework can discover CheckCite programmatically.

input_formats.pdf: Portable Document Format. Requires a running GROBID instance for reference parsing.
input_formats.tex: LaTeX source. References are read from the companion `.bib` file.
input_formats.bib: BibTeX bibliography. Forces 'quick' mode (no citing context).
input_formats.txt: Plain text with inline references. Best-effort parsing.

metadata.VALID: The reference exists in scholarly databases and its metadata matches.
metadata.FABRICATED: The reference could not be resolved to any scholarly database, was retracted, or its metadata mismatches a real paper (chimera citation).
metadata.UNVERIFIABLE: Insufficient database coverage to reach a confident metadata verdict; flagged for human review.

claim.SUPPORTED: The cited paper's content supports the citing sentence(s).
claim.CONTRADICTS: The cited paper says something materially different from at least one citing sentence.
claim.NEUTRAL: The cited paper does not directly address the citing sentence — same general topic, but no entailment.
claim.UNVERIFIABLE: Claim verification could not run (paywalled, agent error, or no substantive citing sentence).

integration_hints.agent_framework: Register as a REST tool. For long papers use the async flow: POST /api/v1/jobs, then poll GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} until status is 'done'. Output schema: PaperReport JSON (see openapi_url). Rendering: results are a list of cards; the existing Gradio UI at `/` can be embedded via iframe if a native renderer is not required.
integration_hints.mcp_server: Two patterns are supported. (1) Short paper: wrap POST /api/v1/verify as a synchronous tool call. (2) Long paper: wrap submit_job + get_job with a small polling loop inside the MCP adapter; expose the combined operation as a single MCP tool that returns when status is terminal.
integration_hints.langchain: Expose as `StructuredTool`. For small papers call /api/v1/verify; for larger ones call /api/v1/jobs and have the tool poll internally. Return the JSON-serialised PaperReport as the tool output.
